status: Sparse native capability verified; dense timing holdouts have visible tail variability, not a claim of universally equal or improved performance.
baseline: Public native SparseSet Transform binding refused startup with ARA0934; actual fixture now succeeds. Baseline was guarded, not a silent public misfilter.
implementation: Retain dense table iteration; exact sparse archetype membership, contiguous run coalescing, bounded worker packets and deterministic serial command playback.
verification: 17lib tests, actual20k-row CLR sparse/churn/filter/undo/command-order test, all-target ara-script clippy, independent unsafe/storage review and workspace formatting passed.
sparse_scope: 50k selected rows in both shapes: aligned50k live; interleaved100k live with sparse filters and table holes. Real managed RefQuery over native sparse Transform+dense physics. Not a before/after speedup or Unity comparison. Metadata retains per physical run records; fragmented storage has extra setup/callback cost.
dense_scope: Frozen existing bfa462… executable versus current178fba… query tick, same arithmetic and exact output bits/ticks.1mrows,15poolworkers+caller, cold/hot separately, two reversed rounds; invalid interrupted reverse attempt retained and excluded.
dense_result_limits: Cold p50+0.6–0.7%; hot p50-1.8–3.3%. Round1cold p95 increases0.320→0.391ms, unresolved tail variability; do not call this an established zero-regression result. Background tasks/load/power are recorded; before/after guards cannot exclude mid-run activity.

sparse.scope: Ara CPU preparation/host feature experiment; no Unity, shipping frame or universal superiority claim.
sparse.method: Two fresh-process rounds with reversed order, nice10. Kernel samples exclude setup/verification; separate untimed Rust allocation counts. Resource guards before/after cannot prove continuous absence of interference. Worker arguments are pool workers plus a participating caller, not total hardware cores.
